docs.title: Odoo Operator
docs.text:
The Odoo Operator runs Odoo on Kubernetes. You describe an instance in one OdooDeployment, and the operator does the rest:

  • it creates or adopts the PostgreSQL database;
  • it installs the modules you list, in a Job, before Odoo starts;
  • it renders odoo.conf from the spec;
  • it runs the Deployment, Services and filestore volume;
  • it upgrades the database when the image changes, or when you ask it to;
  • it serves a maintenance page while Odoo is installed, upgraded or started;
  • it backs up the database and filestore to S3, SFTP, NFS or a volume, and restores them in place, with an undo.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
• Getting started: install the operator and run the sample.
  • Lifecycle: the phases an instance goes through.
  • How backups work, then set up a store.
  • API reference: every field of every resource.
  • Metrics reference: every series on /metrics.

docs.title: Install the operator
docs.text:
Apply the release bundle; it installs the CRDs and runs the manager in odoo-operator-system:

kubectl apply -f https://github.com/MohanadAbugharbia/odoo-operator/releases/latest/download/install.yaml

docs.title: Run the sample
docs.text:
The repository's samples install CloudNativePG, a one-instance PostgreSQL cluster, its credentials and an OdooDeployment in the odoo-sample namespace. From a clone of the repository:

kubectl apply -k config/samples/
kubectl -n odoo-sample get odoodeployment -w

The instance goes through Pending and Initializing (its init Job installs the modules) to Running; Lifecycle explains each phase. Read the sample's comments for what each field does, and the API reference for every field.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Upgrade Odoo to a new image.
  • Set up a backup store and take backups.
  • Turn on the maintenance page.
  • Scrape the metrics.

docs.title: How backups work
docs.text: This page explains what a backup is and where it goes. The guides show how to set up a store, take and schedule backups, restore and run restore drills.

docs.title: Stores and repositories
docs.text: Every store holds restic repositories, one per instance under <path>/<namespace>/<deployment>/, encrypted with the key in encryptionKeySecret (keep a copy of it outside the cluster: without it no backup can be read). The kinds of store and their settings are in Set up a backup store.

docs.title: What a backup holds
docs.text: A backup is one restic snapshot holding dump.sql (a plain pg_dump taken with a pg_dump of the server's major), manifest.json (Odoo's own format, plus an operator key) and the filestore/, so it is also what Odoo's database manager restores. Online backups run beside Odoo: the dump, the attachment list and the row counts all come from one database snapshot, so they agree with each other. Files that disappeared from the filestore since (Odoo's attachment cleanup) are taken from the previous backup; attachments in neither are listed in status.missingFileNames and the backup ends CompletedWithWarnings. An online backup waits up to two hours for Odoo's filestore cleanup cron to finish when it is running or due within ten minutes (phase WaitingForFilestoreCleanup). With a ReadWriteOncePod data volume, or consistency: Offline, Odoo is stopped while the backup runs.

docs.title: Phases of an OdooBackup
docs.text:
OdooBackup phase Meaning Pending Waiting for the instance: one backup, restore or cleanup runs at a time, and backups wait for init, upgrades and rollouts. WaitingForFilestoreCleanup Odoo's filestore cleanup runs or is due; tried again every two minutes. Running The Job runs. Completed / CompletedWithWarnings status.snapshotID holds it. PartiallyCompleted The backup is in the first store, but a copy to another store failed; status.copies says why. Failed status.message names the step that failed and the Job to read.

Deleting an OdooBackup does not delete the snapshot, and deleting an instance never deletes its backups.

docs.title: The backup image
docs.text: The Jobs run ghcr.io/mohanadabugharbia/odoo-operator-backup at the operator's own tag (derived from the operator's image; --backup-image overrides it). It carries the PostgreSQL 14–18 clients, restic, rclone and the odoo-backup agent, and runs as the instance's pod security context with no service account token.

docs.title: Databases
docs.text:
How the operator decides whether it owns an instance's database, and when it may drop it.

  • On the first reconcile the operator looks the database up. If it exists it is adopted (status.database.provisionedBy: external). If it is missing and spec.database.createPolicy is IfNotExists (default) the operator creates it — CREATE DATABASE … ENCODING 'unicode' LC_COLLATE 'C' LC_CTYPE 'C' TEMPLATE template0, the same shape Odoo uses — and tags it with the comment odoo-operator:<namespace>/<name> (provisionedBy: operator).
  • spec.database.deletionPolicy: Delete adds the finalizer odoo.abugharbia.com/database. On deletion the operator stops the pods and drops the database only if it recorded provisionedBy: operator and the database comment still equals its tag. A CR pointing at a pre-existing database never drops it, whatever the policy says.
  • spec.database.name (and nameFromSecret) are immutable so a rename can never orphan or drop the wrong database.
  • spec.odooFilestore.deletionPolicy works the same way for the filestore PVC (Retain by default).

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
An OdooDeployment moves through status.phase:

Phase Meaning Pending The database connection or the database itself is not settled yet (see the Degraded condition for the reason). Initializing The <name>-init Job installs spec.modules (-i, with --load-language from spec.config.loadLanguages) on spec.image. No Deployment exists yet. Upgrading The new image has been pulled once (see Upgrades); the Deployment is scaled to zero and a <name>-upgrade-<hash> Job runs -i <new modules> / -u <spec.upgrade.modules> on it. Running The Deployment runs status.appliedImage; Ready is True once the requested replicas are available (or spec.replicas is 0). BackingUp An offline backup runs; Odoo is stopped (see How backups work). An online backup leaves the phase alone. Restoring An OdooRestore runs; Odoo is stopped until it finishes. Failed A maintenance Job failed. Inspect it with kubectl logs job/<name>; deleting the Job retries it.

status.currentInitJob.startedAt records when the running Job was created and status.lastMaintenanceDuration how long the last successful upgrade took.

Conditions: Ready, DatabaseReady, Initialized and Degraded (True only when something is wrong; its reason names the problem, e.g. DatabaseMissing, InitJobFailed, QuotaExceeded, ImagePullFailed, DatabaseDropFailed).

The <name>-http and <name>-poll Services are created on the first reconcile, before the database and the init Job, so an Ingress pointing at them can be applied together with the CR. They have no endpoints until the Deployment's pods are ready, unless the maintenance page is enabled.

docs.title: Continuous integration
docs.text:
.github/workflows/ci.yml runs on pull requests and on pushes to main. Its first job, Changes, decides which of the others run, so a pull request pays only for the tests its change needs:

Job What it runs Runs on a pull request Runs on main Unit and envtest make test (the envtest suites against a real API server), a check that api/v1/zz_generated.deepcopy.go, config/crd and config/rbac are in sync with the types, and a make build-installer of the release bundle when anything but docs changed when anything but docs changed Lint make lint (golangci-lint) when anything but docs changed when anything but docs changed Backup on PostgreSQL 16–18 hack/backup-it.sh once per major when backup code changed, or with full-ci or backup-ci when anything but docs changed Backup e2e (kind) hack/backup-e2e.sh when backup code changed, or with full-ci or backup-ci when anything but docs changed Images pushes the operator and backup images (amd64 and arm64) tagged sha-<head sha> and pr-<number>, to try a branch on a real cluster with full-ci or images-ci, and only from this repository never
  • Docs means docs/, Markdown files, mkdocs.yml, LICENSE and the Docs workflow. A docs-only change skips every job here.
  • Backup code is the list in the backup filter of the Changes job: the backup agent and its image, the backup and restore types, CRDs and RBAC, the backup controllers and the instance work queue, schedules, go.mod and go.sum, and ci.yml itself. A backup-related change outside that list is still caught by the full run on main; add the path to the filter when that happens.
  • Labels. full-ci runs everything, backup-ci the backup suite and images-ci the images. Adding one of them runs CI again with it, and the newer run replaces the one in progress. Other labels do not start CI.
  • A skipped job counts as passed, so these jobs can be required checks.
  • The Changes job's summary says what ran and why.

.github/workflows/docs.yml builds this site on every pull request and publishes it; see Writing the docs.

docs.title: Test results
docs.text:
The test job runs go test with -json and renders the event stream into a Markdown report with hack/test-summary.py. The report goes to the job summary on every run and, on pull requests, into a single sticky comment that is rewritten in place each time (header go-test-results), so a PR always shows the state of its latest run rather than a trail of comments. The full stream and the coverage profile (plus a rendered coverage.html) are uploaded as artifacts for seven days, and the report links to both.

Two details of the count are worth knowing when reading it:

  • Ginkgo suites are counted in specs, not in Go tests. internal/controller and internal/controller/reconcileloops each expose one Go test to the toolchain (TestControllers) that carries the whole suite, so counting the stream as-is would report 2 tests for ~70 specs. Where a package's output carries Ginkgo's own Ran N of M Specs summary, those numbers are used and the wrapper test is not counted.
  • Only leaf tests count. A table-driven parent with subtests contributes its subtests, not itself.

A package that fails without a failing test — a build error, a panic outside a test, a TestMain failure — is reported as a failure with its output, not silently dropped: go test -json reports a build failure as a separate event shape that names no package.

To get the same report locally:

make test-summary   # writes go-test.json, cover.out and test-summary.md

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• go version v1.25.0+
  • docker version 17.03+.
  • kubectl version v1.28.0+.
  • Access to a Kubernetes v1.28.0+ cluster.

docs.title: Running the tests
docs.text:
make test

This runs the unit suites and the envtest ones (the Kubernetes binaries are downloaded on demand). Coverage is written to cover.out and measured with -coverpkg across every shipped package, so a helper exercised by another package's suite is credited to it; measuring per-package instead understated the project by roughly 25 points.

The internal/database tests that need a real PostgreSQL skip unless one is configured, because they assert the SQL the provisioner emits, the COMMENT that marks operator-owned databases and the refusal to drop a database carrying somebody else's comment. CI starts a postgres:16 service for them. To run them locally against any throwaway server:

TEST_PG_HOST=127.0.0.1 TEST_PG_PORT=5432 \
TEST_PG_USER=postgres TEST_PG_PASSWORD=postgres make test

The backup agent's real-service tests (internal/backup/agent) skip without TEST_BACKUP_PG_HOST (the same variables with a BACKUP_ infix), because they also need restic, rclone and the client tools of the server's major. hack/backup-it.sh runs them inside the backup image against PostgreSQL, an SFTP server and an S3 server it starts in Docker: fidelity of a round trip, the repair from the previous backup, undo, cleanup, and a failure or crash injected at every step of a restore, which must then either leave the live data untouched or finish when run again.

PG_MAJOR=17 hack/backup-it.sh

hack/backup-e2e.sh backs up, restores and undoes a real Odoo in a kind cluster through an S3 store and a PVC store. CI runs both.

make test-e2e additionally needs Docker and kind, and is not part of CI.

docs.title: Deploy a build on a cluster
docs.text:
Build and push your image to the location specified by IMG:

make docker-build docker-push IMG=<some-registry>/odoo-operator:tag

NOTE: This image ought to be published in the personal registry you specified. And it is required to have access to pull the image from the working environment. Make sure you have the proper permission to the registry if the above commands don’t work.

Install the CRDs into the cluster:

make install

Deploy the Manager to the cluster with the image specified by IMG:

make deploy IMG=<some-registry>/odoo-operator:tag

NOTE: If you encounter RBAC errors, you may need to grant yourself cluster-admin privileges or be logged in as admin.

Create instances of your solution You can apply the samples (examples) from the config/sample:

kubectl apply -k config/samples/

NOTE: Ensure that the samples has default values to test it out.

docs.title: Uninstall it
docs.text:
Delete the instances (CRs) from the cluster:

kubectl delete -k config/samples/

Delete the APIs(CRDs) from the cluster:

make uninstall

UnDeploy the controller from the cluster:

make undeploy

The operator is built with Kubebuilder; its book explains the project layout and the make targets.

docs.title: Writing the docs
docs.text:
The site is built with MkDocs and Material for MkDocs from the docs/ folder, and published to GitHub Pages at https://odoo-operator.abugharbia.com/. A change in behaviour and the change to its page go in the same pull request.

The README stays short: what the operator is, the install command and links here. Usage, operations and internals belong on this site, so a feature pull request edits its page under docs/, not the README.

docs.title: Build and preview locally
docs.text:
make docs-serve    # http://127.0.0.1:8000, reloads on every save
make docs-build    # what CI runs: fails on any warning, such as a broken link

Both create a Python virtual environment under bin/docs-venv from docs/requirements.txt on first use.

docs.title: Generated pages
docs.text:
docs/reference/api.md and docs/reference/metrics.md are generated; do not edit them. After changing a type in api/v1 or a metric in internal/metrics, run:

make docs-reference

and commit the result. CI fails a pull request whose generated pages are stale.

  • The API reference comes from the Go types and their comments, through crd-ref-docs (hack/docs/crd-ref-docs.yaml).
  • The metrics reference comes from the metrics the operator registers (metrics.Reference, written out by hack/docs). A new metric must be added to the registered list in internal/metrics/metrics.go, or to the Collector, to be exported at all, so it cannot be left out of the page.

docs.title: Preview a pull request
docs.text:
Add the docs-preview label to a pull request. The site of that pull request is then published at https://odoo-operator.abugharbia.com/pr-preview/pr-<number>/, a comment on the pull request links to it, and every push updates it. Removing the label or closing the pull request deletes the preview.

Pull requests from forks get no preview: their workflows cannot write to the repository. Every pull request, labelled or not, still builds the site.

docs.title: Published versions
docs.text:
When Published as A push to main dev A release its major.minor (for example 0.6), also latest, the default

mike keeps one folder per version on the gh-pages branch, and the version picker in the header switches between them.

docs.title: Set up a backup store
docs.text:
An OdooBackupStore says where backups go. Every store holds encrypted restic repositories, one per instance under <path>/<namespace>/<deployment>/, encrypted with the key in encryptionKeySecret.

Keep the encryption key

Keep a copy of the key in encryptionKeySecret outside the cluster: without it no backup can be read.

apiVersion: odoo.abugharbia.com/v1
kind: OdooBackupStore
metadata:
  name: offsite
  namespace: shop
spec:
  s3:                                 # or sftp, nfs, pvc: exactly one
    endpoint: https://s3.example.com
    bucket: odoo-backups
    path: production
    credentialsSecret: { name: s3-credentials }   # AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  encryptionKeySecret: { name: backup-key, key: password }

docs.title: Kinds of store
docs.text: Kind Fields Secret s3 endpoint (empty for AWS), region, bucket, path, forcePathStyle credentialsSecret: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY sftp host, port (22), user, path sshSecret: the private key under id_ed25519 or ssh-privatekey, and known_hosts (the server's host key; nothing else is trusted) nfs server, path pvc claimName, subPath

docs.title: SFTP keys
docs.text:
The SFTP private key can be any unencrypted Ed25519, ECDSA or RSA key, in OpenSSH or PEM format; a key with a passphrase does not work. The key name only says where the key is, not its type: id_ed25519 is read first, and ssh-privatekey is the key of Secrets of type kubernetes.io/ssh-auth. known_hosts takes the server's host key of any type:

ssh-keyscan -p 22 backup.example.com > known_hosts
kubectl -n shop create secret generic my-odoo-sftp \
  --from-file=id_ed25519=$HOME/.ssh/backup_key --from-file=known_hosts

Check the scanned key against the one the server's provider shows before you trust it.

docs.title: Probes
docs.text:
The operator probes each store with a short Job that writes, reads and deletes a file (.odoo-operator-probe-<random>), on every change to the store or its Secrets and every six hours. kubectl get odoobackupstore shows Ready; a store that fails says why in its Ready condition and in an event, and is probed again every two minutes until it passes. The last failed probe's Job is kept for its log.

To keep a store healthy over time, check and prune it on a schedule.

docs.title: Take and schedule backups
docs.text:
Backups need three objects: a store, the instance pointing at it, and a backup.

apiVersion: odoo.abugharbia.com/v1
kind: OdooBackupStore
metadata:
  name: offsite
  namespace: shop
spec:
  s3:                                 # or sftp, nfs, pvc: exactly one
    endpoint: https://s3.example.com
    bucket: odoo-backups
    path: production
    credentialsSecret: { name: s3-credentials }   # AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  encryptionKeySecret: { name: backup-key, key: password }
---
# in the OdooDeployment
spec:
  backup:
    stores: [offsite]
    consistency: Online               # default; Offline stops Odoo while it runs
---
apiVersion: odoo.abugharbia.com/v1
kind: OdooBackup
metadata:
  name: my-odoo-2026-10-17
  namespace: shop
spec:
  odooDeployment: my-odoo

Once a store is Ready, creating an OdooBackup takes a backup; How backups work explains what it holds and the phases it goes through.

docs.title: Schedules and retention
docs.text:
deleted after each backup:

spec:
  backup:
    stores: [offsite, cold]           # the first is written; the others get copies
    schedule: "0 3 * * *"             # cron or @daily; empty (default) = no scheduled backups
    timeZone: Europe/Berlin           # of the schedules and the retention periods (default UTC)
    retention:                        # defaults: daily 7, weekly 4, monthly 12
      daily: 7
      weekly: 4
      monthly: 12
      within: 2d                      # also keep everything from the last 2 days (y, m, d, h)
      manual: 10                      # newest manual and pre-upgrade backups kept; 0 (default) keeps all
    drill:
      schedule: "0 5 * * 0"           # [restore drill](drills.md)

A scheduled backup is an ordinary OdooBackup named <instance>-<yyyymmdd-hhmm> (the time in timeZone) that waits in the instance's queue like any other. A time missed while the operator was down is taken once when it is back; a time that comes while the previous scheduled backup is still unfinished is skipped with an event. status.backup shows the last and next scheduled times, and the BackupSchedule condition reports a schedule that cannot be read.

Retention runs in the backup Job, after the new backup is verified. The keep rules are restic's (last, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, yearly, within, with restic's meaning), but the periods are counted in timeZone, and they apply to scheduled backups; manual and pre-upgrade backups each keep their newest manual. Never deleted: the newest backup, a backup with spec.keep: true (it does not use up a slot of the rules either), a snapshot an unfinished restore needs, and snapshots the operator did not take. The OdooBackups of deleted snapshots are deleted too; a retention that fails leaves the backup Completed with a warning. retention.keepAll: true turns it off. Deleting the snapshot frees no space by itself: the store's prune does.

docs.title: Copies
docs.text: Each backup is copied (restic copy) to every store after the first in spec.backup.stores, in the same Job, and retention runs in each copy too. A store that is missing or not ready, or a copy that fails, leaves the backup PartiallyCompleted with status.copies saying why; the backup in the first store is still good. A restore (or drill) whose backup's store is not ready restores a copy from a ready store instead, with an event saying so. Stores may use different kinds and different encryption keys.

docs.title: Restore drills
docs.text: A drill proves the newest backup can be restored, without touching the instance: on spec.backup.drill.schedule it waits in the instance's queue, then one Job restores the newest finished backup into a scratch database <db>_drill_<suffix> and a scratch filestore on an emptyDir (never the data volume), runs the same checks as a restore, has the backup's own Odoo image read it (odoo shell -d <db>_drill_<suffix>, run through sh: Odoo loads its registry, reads records of core models and reads attachments from the scratch filestore), and drops the scratch database. Odoo keeps serving throughout. The outcome is in status.backup.lastDrill (lastSuccessfulDrillTime keeps the last pass); a failed drill keeps its Job (kubectl logs job/<name> --all-containers). The scratch filestore needs node disk the size of the filestore; drill.scratchSizeLimit caps it.

docs.title: Maintenance page
docs.text:
With spec.maintenancePage.enabled: true, a browser opening the instance while Odoo cannot answer gets a status page instead of a blank screen:

spec:
  maintenancePage:
    enabled: true
    title: My Shop            # default "Odoo"
    titleTranslations:
      ar: متجري
    accentColor: "#f2800d"    # default "#714b67"
    logo: data:image/svg+xml;base64,…   # optional, data URIs only
  • Whenever Odoo's Deployment has no available replica (first setup, an upgrade, a restart) and spec.replicas is not 0, the operator runs a <name>-maintenance Deployment (one pod, 10m CPU / 32Mi) and points the <name>-http Service's selector at it. Once Odoo has an available replica the selector moves back and the page scales to zero. The <name>-poll Service always stays on Odoo.
  • The pod runs the operator's own image (odoo-operator maintenance-page), so there is nothing extra to build or pin. The operator reads its image from its own pod, retrying on each reconcile until it succeeds (a failure shows as a MaintenancePageImageUnknown warning event on the OdooDeployment); --maintenance-page-image overrides it.
  • The page needs no access to the API server: after every reconcile the operator writes what the page shows into the <name>-maintenance ConfigMap, which the pod mounts (no ServiceAccount token). On each change it also stamps the status hash on the page pods (odoo.abugharbia.com/maintenance-status), which makes the kubelet refresh the mount at once instead of on its next periodic sync, up to a minute later.
  • It answers like a server that is down, so Odoo's own clients keep their offline behaviour: a page navigation (Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate) gets the page with status 503, and every other request (RPC, assets, /web/health, service worker fetches) gets an empty 503. Nothing is cacheable.
  • The page shows the phase as steps (preparing the database, installing, updating, starting), the elapsed time and, for upgrades, an estimate from status.lastMaintenanceDuration. It polls /__maintenance/status.json and /web/health every 3 seconds, and reopens the URL that was asked for as soon as Odoo answers. A failed Job shows only "Please contact your administrator"; the reason stays in the CR's conditions and events.
  • English or Arabic (right to left) is picked from the browser's Accept-Language; it follows the device's light or dark mode, and loads no external fonts or scripts.

docs.title: Monitoring and alerts
docs.text: The manager serves /metrics (by default on :8443, HTTPS, with Kubernetes authentication and authorization; --metrics-bind-address=:8080 --metrics-secure=false serves plain HTTP instead). Besides the controller-runtime defaults (controller_runtime_reconcile_*, workqueue_*, rest_client_*, Go and process metrics) it exports the series in the metrics reference.

docs.title: Alerts
docs.text: config/prometheus/backup-alerts.yaml holds example alerts on these metrics (stale or failed backups, failed copies, restores and drills, stores that are not ready or fail their check or prune). Adjust the staleness thresholds to your schedules.

docs.title: Restore and undo
docs.text:
A restore replaces the instance's database and filestore in place:

apiVersion: odoo.abugharbia.com/v1
kind: OdooRestore
metadata:
  name: back-to-friday
  namespace: shop
spec:
  odooDeployment: my-odoo
  backup: my-odoo-2026-10-17        # or snapshotID: <id> in the instance's store
  keepPrevious: 72h                 # default spec.backup.restore.keepPrevious (72h)

Odoo is stopped; the backup is loaded into <db>_restore_<suffix> and filestore/<db>_restore_<suffix> beside the live data and checked (every table's row count against the backup, every attachment's file, a sample of files against their checksum). Only then are the names swapped: the live data becomes <db>_prev_<suffix> and the restored data takes its place, and Odoo starts on the image recorded in the backup. A restore that fails before the swap leaves the live data untouched (Failed); one that fails during the swap is retried until it finishes, with Odoo stopped and the instance Degraded (RestoreIncomplete). A restore takes precedence over everything else and replaces a failed upgrade Job, which makes it the way back from a failed upgrade. Modules in spec.modules that the backup lacks are installed again afterwards. If spec.image differs from the backup's image the usual upgrade follows; set spec.image to the backup's image first to stay on it.

docs.title: Undo a restore
docs.text:
The replaced data is kept until status.previous.keptUntil, then deleted. Until then the restore can be undone:

spec:
  odooDeployment: my-odoo
  undo: back-to-friday

Only the latest restore can be undone. Deleting an OdooRestore deletes the data it kept.

docs.title: Check and prune a store
docs.text:
On their own schedules a store's repositories are checked (restic check) and pruned (restic prune, which frees the space of deleted backups):

spec:                                 # OdooBackupStore
  check:
    schedule: "0 4 * * 0"
    readDataParts: 7                  # each check reads 1/7 of the data, all of it over 7 checks;
                                      # 1 = everything every time, 0 = structure only
  prune:
    schedule: "0 2 * * 6"
  timeZone: Europe/Berlin

One Job runs at a time per store, prune first when both are due, over the repositories of every instance in the namespace that lists the store. The outcome is in status.lastCheck and status.lastPrune (with the part read, the repositories and what they hold); a failed task keeps its Job for its log and warns. A backup that starts while a prune holds a repository's lock waits up to half an hour for it.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
Remove your instances first, while the operator still runs: it is the operator that applies their deletion policies.

kubectl delete odoodeployments --all --all-namespaces

What stays behind depends on each instance's policies:

  • The database is dropped only with spec.database.deletionPolicy: Delete, and only when the operator created it (see Databases).
  • The filestore volume is kept unless spec.odooFilestore.deletionPolicy is Delete.
  • Backups are never deleted: deleting an instance or an OdooBackup leaves the snapshots in their stores.

Then remove the operator, its CRDs and RBAC:

kubectl delete -f https://github.com/MohanadAbugharbia/odoo-operator/releases/latest/download/install.yaml

Deleting the CRDs deletes every remaining OdooDeployment, OdooBackup, OdooRestore and OdooBackupStore with them. Use the release you installed if it is not the latest.

docs.title: Upgrade Odoo
docs.text:
An upgrade runs Odoo's -u on the database in a Job, with the Deployment scaled to zero, whenever the image changes or you ask for it.

  • spec.upgrade.onImageChange: true (default): every spec.image change runs an upgrade Job with -u <spec.upgrade.modules> before the Deployment rolls to the new image. New entries in spec.modules are installed in the same Job.
  • Empty spec.upgrade.modules rolls the new image without a Job.
  • A new image is pulled before anything stops. When spec.image changes on a running instance, a short <name>-image-<hash> Job runs <odooCommand> --version on it first, without the filestore or the config. Only once it succeeds is the Deployment scaled down (or rolled). Until then the old image keeps serving; if the image cannot be pulled Degraded is ImagePullFailed (or ImageCheckFailed when it pulled but did not run), and a later spec.image replaces the check. This is what keeps an instance up when its image tag is published before the image is pushed, or never is.
  • An init or upgrade Job whose pod cannot pull its image is reported as ImagePullFailed. If spec.image changes meanwhile, the Job is replaced by one for the new image: its container never started, so nothing touched the database.
  • For production set onImageChange: false and bump spec.upgrade.token to run the upgrade on demand.
  • spec.jobs bounds the Jobs (activeDeadlineSeconds, ttlSecondsAfterFinished, backoffLimit).

A failed upgrade can be rolled back by restoring a backup: a restore replaces a failed upgrade Job.

docs.title: Upgrading the operator
docs.text: Read the notes of every version between the one you run and the one you install.

• list_db is now False by default and dbfilter = ^<db_name>$ is rendered, so an instance only sees its own database. Set spec.config.listDb: true (and optionally dbFilter) to keep the database manager.
  • spec.database.ssl is rendered as db_sslmode = require / disable (previously it was ignored and Odoo used prefer).
  • spec.database.name and spec.database.nameFromSecret are immutable.
  • spec.replicas, spec.config.workers, maxCronThreads, withoutDemo and proxyMode are pointer fields: 0 and false are now honoured.
  • Existing CRs roll their pods once (new labels, config-hash annotation, probes) and adopt the running image as status.appliedImage without a Job. Their database is adopted as external and is never dropped.
  • The OperatorDegraded/OperatorSucceeded conditions are replaced by Ready, DatabaseReady, Initialized and Degraded.
  • The admin and config Secrets and both Services are now owned by the CR and are garbage collected with it.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The operator renders odoo.conf from spec.config and spec.database; every field is in the API reference.

docs.title: Container command
docs.text: spec.odooCommand (default ["odoo"]) plus -c /opt/odoo/odoo.conf becomes the container command, which replaces the image ENTRYPOINT. Images whose entrypoint script injects database flags (e.g. the official image's entrypoint.sh) are bypassed on purpose: the operator's rendered odoo.conf is the only configuration source. The image's own addons_path and server_wide_modules must therefore be re-expressed in spec.config.extraAddonsPaths and spec.config.serverWideModules.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
The manager serves these on /metrics beside the controller-runtime defaults; Monitoring and alerts shows how to scrape them.

  • Series marked scrape time are read from the status of every OdooDeployment and OdooBackupStore when Prometheus scrapes. Only the elected leader reports them, and a deleted object disappears on the next scrape.
  • The others count events, each once, on the reconcile that causes it: a Job that stays failed, an image that keeps failing to pull or a drop that keeps failing is not counted again on every requeue. The per-OdooDeployment counters start at 0 and are removed once the OdooDeployment is gone.
Metric Type Labels Description odoo_operator_backup_duration_seconds histogram kind How long backups that succeeded took, from the start of their first Job to completion. odoo_operator_backup_enabled gauge namespace, name 1 when the OdooDeployment takes scheduled backups (spec.backup.schedule is set). (scrape time) odoo_operator_backup_last_copy_failed gauge namespace, name, store Per copy store, 1 when the instance's most recently finished backup could not be copied there. (scrape time) odoo_operator_backup_last_failed gauge namespace, name 1 when the instance's most recently finished backup failed. (scrape time) odoo_operator_backup_last_size_bytes gauge namespace, name, part Sizes of the instance's newest successful backup: part is database, filestore or added (new data uploaded). (scrape time) odoo_operator_backup_last_success_timestamp_seconds gauge namespace, name When the instance's newest successful backup (Completed or CompletedWithWarnings) completed, as a Unix timestamp. (scrape time) odoo_operator_backup_missing_files gauge namespace, name Attachments the database refers to that the instance's newest successful backup could not include. (scrape time) odoo_operator_backup_store_ready gauge namespace, store 1 when the OdooBackupStore's last probe could write, read and delete a file. (scrape time) odoo_operator_backup_store_stored_bytes gauge namespace, store What the instance repositories in the store hold together, as of its latest check or prune. (scrape time) odoo_operator_backup_store_task_last_failed gauge namespace, store, task 1 when the store's latest check or prune (task) failed. (scrape time) odoo_operator_backup_store_task_last_timestamp_seconds gauge namespace, store, task When the store's latest check or prune (task) finished, as a Unix timestamp. (scrape time) odoo_operator_backups_total counter kind, result Backups (OdooBackup) that finished, by kind (manual, scheduled, pre-upgrade) and result (succeeded, failed). odoo_operator_build_info gauge version Always 1; the version label is the running operator release. odoo_operator_database_operations_total counter operation, result Database create, adopt and drop operations, by result (succeeded, failed, refused). A failure is counted once until it clears. odoo_operator_deployment_condition gauge namespace, name, type, status, reason Always 1, one series per status condition; status is true, false or unknown. (scrape time) odoo_operator_deployment_condition_last_transition_timestamp_seconds gauge namespace, name, type When each status condition last changed status, as a Unix timestamp. (scrape time) odoo_operator_deployment_database_ready gauge namespace, name, provisioned_by 1 while the DatabaseReady condition is true; provisioned_by is operator or external. (scrape time) odoo_operator_deployment_image_pending gauge namespace, name 1 while spec.image differs from status.appliedImage (an image check or upgrade is pending). (scrape time) odoo_operator_deployment_info gauge namespace, name, image, applied_image, database Always 1; the labels are the OdooDeployment's spec.image, status.appliedImage and database name. (scrape time) odoo_operator_deployment_job_start_timestamp_seconds gauge namespace, name, kind When the running init or upgrade Job was created, as a Unix timestamp. Absent while no Job runs. (scrape time) odoo_operator_deployment_last_upgrade_duration_seconds gauge namespace, name status.lastMaintenanceDuration: how long the last successful upgrade Job took. (scrape time) odoo_operator_deployment_phase gauge namespace, name, phase 1 for the OdooDeployment's current status.phase, 0 for the others. (scrape time) odoo_operator_deployment_replicas_desired gauge namespace, name spec.replicas: Odoo pods the OdooDeployment runs outside maintenance. (scrape time) odoo_operator_image_pull_failures_total counter namespace, name Times a new image could not be pulled, counted once each time an OdooDeployment becomes Degraded with ImagePullFailed. odoo_operator_job_duration_seconds histogram kind, result How long init and upgrade Jobs that succeeded or failed took, from creation to completion or failure. odoo_operator_jobs_total counter namespace, name, kind, result Init and upgrade Jobs that finished, by result (succeeded, failed, superseded). Each Job is counted once. odoo_operator_maintenance_page_publish_errors_total counter namespace, name Failed attempts to publish an OdooDeployment's status to its maintenance page. odoo_operator_restore_drill_enabled gauge namespace, name 1 when the OdooDeployment runs restore drills (spec.backup.drill.schedule is set). (scrape time) odoo_operator_restore_drill_last_failed gauge namespace, name 1 when the instance's latest restore drill failed. (scrape time) odoo_operator_restore_drill_last_success_timestamp_seconds gauge namespace, name When a restore drill of the instance last passed, as a Unix timestamp. Absent until one passes. (scrape time) odoo_operator_restore_last_failed gauge namespace, name 1 when the instance's most recently finished OdooRestore failed. (scrape time) odoo_operator_restores_total counter mode, result In-place restores (OdooRestore) that finished, by mode (restore, undo) and result (succeeded, failed).
